question: Will the Bundestag pass the 2027 German federal budget before 2027?

calls.reasoning: Base rate: with an intact coalition in a non-election year, German federal budgets are almost always passed in the late-Nov/early-Dec budget week. The 2027 schedule is in place: committee wrap-up session 12-13 Nov 2026, final roll-call vote Fri 27 Nov 2026, with a December sitting week as fallback. Downward adjustment: the Union-SPD coalition is badly strained (2026 government crisis, state-election collapses, Merz approval at 14%, SPD demanding pension/care reform changes, some Union MPs reportedly refusing the current draft), coalition tax talks were deadlocked as of 9 Nov, and the coalition holds only about 328/630 seats. Residual risk is a coalition break or a slip into 2027 like 2024/2025. No prediction market found.
calls.dossier:
- Bundestag official timeline (bundestag.de kw34 explainer, 2026): first reading 8-11 Sep 2026; budget committee wrap-up session (Bereinigungssitzung) Thu 12 Nov 2026 running into early Fri; final debate 24-27 Nov 2026; third-reading roll-call vote on the Haushaltsgesetz 2027 scheduled Fri 27 Nov 2026.
- hib press note 6 Nov 2026: committee is finishing its work, wrap-up session planned for Thursday; no postponement mentioned.
- Tagesspiegel 9 Nov 2026: Union and SPD still in dispute over taxes (plastic tax, sugar tax, electricity tax cut costing about EUR 5bn/yr that Merz wants and Klingbeil opposes, inflation adjustment of income tax brackets); 'the clock is ticking'; Merz/Klingbeil must settle it before Thursday.
- Kurierverlag/news.de Nov 2026: SPD wants to block cuts to housing allowance and child supplement (about EUR 770m); Union demands extra tax relief.
- Berliner Zeitung headline Nov 2026: 'Klingbeil's record budget wobbles: is the Merz coalition facing the traffic-light coalition's fate?' (article not opened).
- Wikipedia '2026 German government crisis' (updated 8 Nov 2026): Spahn resignation July 2026; AfD 43.8% in Saxony-Anhalt (6 Sep); CDU fell below 5% in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern (20 Sep); Merz approval 14%; SPD demanded revisions to pension/care reforms and threatened the 2027 budget; some Union MPs reportedly unwilling to vote for the budget as it stands; coalition technically intact as of late Oct.
- Budget figures: core spending EUR 555.4bn, core net borrowing EUR 118.7bn (about EUR 204bn including special funds); cabinet adopted the draft 6 Jul 2026.
- Coalition seats: about 328 of 630 (CDU/CSU 208 + SPD 120); majority 316.
- Historical: budgets are normally passed in the late-Nov/early-Dec budget week. Exceptions: the 2024 budget slipped to 2 Feb 2024 after the Nov 2023 Constitutional Court ruling; the 2025 budget was never passed in 2024 after the traffic-light coalition collapsed 6 Nov 2024; election-year budgets (e.g. 2018, 2022) were passed the following year.
- Status quo: the final vote is on the calendar for 27 Nov; a December sitting week remains as fallback.
- Resolves off: Bundestag passage of the Budget Act 2027 in final (third) reading; the Bundesrat step is not required.
- Event window: now -> 2027-01-01 00:00 CET per the criteria; as of 10 Nov 2026 the vote is scheduled about 17 days out.
- Searched, not found: any prediction market (Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold none); any official announcement postponing the wrap-up session or the final vote; any outcome of the 12-13 Nov wrap-up session (has not happened yet).

calls.reasoning: Reference class: German federal budgets in years without an election, under a sitting coalition. These have almost always passed in November or December of the year before. The one exception in recent memory is the 2025 budget, which failed when the traffic-light coalition collapsed in November 2024. Base rate is about 90%. For 2027 the schedule is set and on time: cabinet draft July 6, first reading September 8, the Budget Committee's final session November 12-13, plenary debate November 24-27 with the final vote on November 27. December sitting weeks give some room if it slips. The risks are the CDU/CSU-SPD coalition's thin majority and ongoing fights over the sugar and plastic taxes, cold-progression relief, housing allowance and the child supplement. The Federal Audit Office has also questioned a 6.8bn draw from a reserve it says holds no real money. None of these looks like a threat to the coalition. The 2027 schedule is on track: Bereinigungssitzung 12-13 Nov, final roll-call vote 27 Nov 2026, December sitting weeks as fallback. Main risk: the reportedly serious 2026 coalition crisis (low Merz approval, SPD threats over pensions/care, some Union MPs unwilling to vote for the draft) plus deadlocked tax/benefit talks and a ~12-seat majority could produce a break or a slip into 2027 as in 2024/2025. calls.reconciliation: The runs differed mainly on how severe the coalition crisis is. Run 1 cites a Wikipedia 'government crisis' page with SPD budget threats and Union MPs unwilling to vote for the draft; Run 3 found no breakdown threat. I could not verify this without web access. Run 1's details are specific and consistent with the Berliner Zeitung headline about the coalition wobbling, so I treat the crisis as plausibly real and weight collapse risk above Run 3's view. Everyone agrees on the schedule (vote 27 Nov, December fallback) and on the lack of any market. The tax/benefit deadlock is a routine pre-wrap-up fight, and the Audit Office objection carries no near-term legal risk. Net: high base rate, minus roughly a 10% chance of collapse or a slip into 2027.
